tools.name: settings_inspect
tools.description: Inspect supported hub-wide provider fallback settings and installed model capabilities. Never returns credentials.

tools.name: settings_propose
tools.description: Propose a hub-wide fallback change for the person's one-time approval. This never applies the change itself. Do not supply credentials or secrets.

chain.description: Comma-separated installed provider/model hierarchy; empty only when off.

tools.name: orchestrator_capabilities
tools.description: List the providers and models this Backplane can run, the delegation depth limit, and this thread's own provider, model and depth.

tools.name: delegate_task
tools.description: Create a bounded subthread by delegating one task to a child agent of THIS thread, on any provider/model (see orchestrator_capabilities). The child sees only `prompt` of this conversation (no history) and works in this thread's directory; like every thread it has Backplane's instructions and the installed skills (KiStack's KiCad skills, the person's) and uses the one its task matches, so name a skill rather than pasting it. Its result arrives in this thread as a message when it finishes, so end your turn instead of polling; use task_status only when you need it mid-turn. Delegation is limited in depth; children of children are allowed up to the limit.

prompt.description: The complete task for the child, with every detail it needs.

provider.description: claude, codex, grok, muse, antigravity, opencode, pi or omp (default: this thread's).

model.description: Model for the child (default: this thread's).

title.description: Short title for the child thread.

project.description: Bots only, and required for them: the project's name or id (project_list); the child is a thread of its own there that the person can follow.

tools.name: task_status
tools.description: Read a delegated task: state (queued, running, done, failed, cancelled), the child's thread, and its result summary once finished.

tools.name: task_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a running delegated task (stops its child agent). Finished tasks keep their result.

tools.name: thread_list
tools.description: List the threads of this thread's project (id, title, provider, model, turn state, and phase: monitoring while work it owns runs after its turn), newest activity first. With `machine` (machine_list shows them), the threads of that other machine of the person's, whose ids work in the thread tools here; `project` narrows it to one project there.

machine.description: Another machine's name (or link id): list its threads.

project.description: With machine: a project there, by name or id.

tools.name: machine_list
tools.description: List the person's machines linked to this one (this one first), whether each is here or away, and each one's projects with ids you can give thread_launch. A thread elsewhere has an id like <link>~<id>; thread_send, thread_read, thread_wait, thread_interrupt and thread_update take it, so you can work with a thread on any of their machines.

tools.name: thread_read
tools.description: Read a thread's status (including turn state) and available timeline in this project (or on another machine, by its <link>~<id>): messages and tool activity, oldest first (the last `limit` entries). Empty entries alone do not mean stopped or completed; inspect status.turn and status.phase: monitoring means the turn is over but work the thread owns (a background subagent, shell or monitor, or a delegated task) still runs (status.waiting counts it, status.work names it); only complete means nothing is left.

tools.name: thread_send
tools.description: Send a message to another thread in this project, or on another machine by its <link>~<id>. It is delivered at once: an idle thread starts a turn with it, a running turn takes it (Claude at once; Codex, Grok and Muse with their next Backplane tool result, or as a new turn if theirs ends first).

tools.name: thread_launch
tools.description: Create a continuing subthread of this calling thread, with a first message on any provider/model. It nests under its launcher, counts in its subthreads badge, reports back and follows normal auto-settle rules; it can still be opened and messaged on its own. Use subthread false ONLY when the user explicitly requests a top-level conversation. Local subthreads must stay in their launcher’s project; bots and launches on another machine have no local parent. Bots must name the project. Scratch is retired and cannot be a launch target; use a project from machine_list. Answers its threadId. Its reports come to you by themselves, as a message that wakes you: each time its turn ends (completed, failed or interrupted, with its last reply), and at once when it asks the person something; so end your turn instead of polling, and answer it with thread_send. report false launches it without reports; thread_update turns them off or on later. With `machine`, it starts on that other machine of the person's, in its project named by `project` (machine_list).

subthread.description: Nest under this calling thread (default true). False only for an explicitly requested top-level thread; required for cross-project launches.

title.description: A short title (default: from the prompt).

report.description: Whether its turn ends and asks are reported to you (default true).

provider.description: claude, codex, grok, muse, antigravity, opencode, pi or omp (default: the user's default).

project.description: The project's name or id (default: this thread's; bots must give one); on another machine its <link>~<id> from machine_list.

machine.description: Start it on another machine of the person's, in its project of that name (machine_list).

tools.name: thread_update
tools.description: Configure a thread's provider/model between turns without sending a message or starting an agent; answers the saved status. Running turns are rejected. Stopped queued work stays held until a new request or explicit resume. Fresh choices are silent; established history is kept for the next real prompt. With no provider/model: rename with title, regenerate the title with no title, or change a launched thread's reports with report. Give parent alone to explicitly move a thread under a conversation in the same project, or empty to move to top level; this persists ThreadParentSet and wins over its launch relationship. Configuration cannot be combined with title/report/parent.

parent.description: Explicit parent move (same project); empty moves to top level. Use only when asked to move a thread; give without title/report/provider/model.

threadId.description: The thread (default: this one), or its <link>~<id> on another machine.

provider.description: claude, codex, grok, muse, antigravity, opencode, pi or omp. A different provider uses its default model unless model is given; accounts are unchanged.

model.description: Set the selected provider's model; empty selects its default. May be used alone.

title.description: The new title; empty to regenerate it.

report.description: For a thread you launched: whether its reports come to you.

tools.name: thread_wait
tools.description: Wait until a thread in this project has finished its turn, or until timeoutMs passes. Answers its state, whether it is done, and its last reply. For anything longer than a few minutes use wake_on instead and end your turn.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait at most (default 30000, at most 600000).

tools.name: thread_interrupt
tools.description: Stop the running turn of a thread in this project.

tools.name: thread_settle
tools.description: Settle a thread in this project (default: this one): move it out of the active list as done, the same as the Settle button. Use it when the person asks you to settle, once your work is finished.

threadId.description: The thread; this thread when left out.

tools.name: deploy_restart
tools.description: Restart the Backplane hub into a new build safely. Answers at once: the restart waits until no thread is inside a tool call (a build, an edit) and the build lock (/tmp/bp-bend.lock) is free, then goes; every turn it cuts resumes by itself. With stage, a directory holding the built package (backplane, backplane-serve, web/ ...) is swapped into the install first. You are woken after the restart with the new version: end your turn, do not wait.

stage.description: Absolute path of a staged package to install first (default: the files are already in place).

tools.name: deploy_status
tools.description: Whether a deploy_restart waits, who asked, and what it still waits for (tool calls in flight, the build lock); under main, deploy_main's state (the commit building, staged, live).

tools.name: deploy_main
tools.description: Deploy origin/main to this machine's hub: the hub fetches it in its source checkout (setting deploy.repo), builds it in a job of its own and restarts into it safely (as deploy_restart). Answers at once: queued, skipped (origin/main is already in the commit being built, staged or live: the answer names it) or not configured. One build runs at a time; requests during it make one more build of the newest origin/main. When the build ends you are told (commit, version, result): end your turn, do not wait or poll.

tools.name: deploy_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a waiting deploy_restart.

tools.name: viewer_show
tools.description: Show a file in the user's Backplane viewer panel: a .kicad_pcb on the Board tab (kind 3d: the board in 3D), a .kicad_sch on the Schematic tab, and any .step/.stp or .glb on the Mech tab, the 3D design tab (the model turned in 3D, the project's parts in mech/ beside it, their renders a tap away), wherever the file is. Use it after changing a design so the user sees the result; the viewer also follows the file live.

kind.description: board, schematic, 3d (a board in 3D) or mech (a STEP or GLB); default from the extension.

tools.name: kicad_export10
tools.description: Export an outside-project KiCad 10 copy. First returns a compatibility report; force accepts the reported changes. Never opens a GUI.

force.description: Accept changes, including dropping blocked approximations (default false).

tools.name: terminal_open
tools.description: Open a terminal in this chat that runs a command (through the user's shell, in this thread's folder) and that the user sees and types into right in the conversation. Use it to hand the user a small tool: a TUI, a picker, an interactive script, a live monitor, a REPL. It answers the terminal's id at once; when the command ends the terminal stays open at the user's shell. Read its screen with terminal_read; what it shows when the user next writes to you comes with their message. It stops (and greys out, a click restarts it) when the user sends another message, unless they pin it.

command.description: The command line, e.g. python3 tools/pick.py or htop.

title.description: A short title shown above it.

tools.name: terminal_read
tools.description: Read a terminal of this chat: its state (running: the command runs; done N: it ended with status N and the shell is open; stopped or exited N: the terminal is closed) and the text on its screen. waitMs waits until the command ends, up to that long, for a script you want the result of.

waitMs.description: Wait for the command to end, at most this long (default 0, at most 120000).

tools.name: terminal_send
tools.description: Type into a terminal of this chat, as the user would: text is sent as is (\r is Enter, \u0003 is ctrl+c, \u001b[A is Up).

text.description: The bytes to send, as text.

tools.name: terminal_close
tools.description: Stop a terminal of this chat (its program is hung up; the user can start it again).

tools.name: secret_request
tools.description: Ask the person for a secret (an API key, auth key, token or password) without it ever passing through the chat or reaching you: they get a masked box in this chat that names you and your purpose, and the value goes straight into Backplane's vault. Answers {secret, set}; when it is not set yet, end your turn: a message tells you once they saved it. Never ask for a secret in a message.

name.description: A short name for it, e.g. tailscale-bub or github-token (lower case, digits, - _ .).

purpose.description: What you need it for, in one line the person reads.

tools.name: secret_list
tools.description: List the secrets in Backplane's vault as handles: [{secret, set, purpose, usedAt}]. You never get a value.

tools.name: secret_run
tools.description: Run a shell command (in this thread's folder) that uses secrets from the vault without you seeing them: env {VAR: name} puts a secret in the command's environment as $VAR, files {VAR: name} writes it to a private temporary file (removed after) whose path is $VAR, e.g. `tailscale up --auth-key=file:$TS` with files {TS: tailscale-bub}, or `gh auth login --with-token < $GH`. Prefer files over putting $VAR on a command line. Answers {code, stdout, stderr} with every secret masked.

env.description: Environment variable name to secret name.

files.description: Environment variable (gets the file's path) to secret name.

cwd.description: Folder to run in (default this thread's).

timeout.description: Seconds before it is stopped (default 120, at most 600).

tools.name: wake_on
tools.description: Subscribe to a local thread, work id, PR or absolute file path. A matching event posts a message in your thread and wakes you; end your turn instead of polling. Thread targets elsewhere are not supported yet.

target.description: Thread/work id, owner/repo#N (or #N in a project), or absolute path.

note.description: Include this reminder in the wake message.

tools.name: wake_list
tools.description: List your wake subscriptions.

tools.name: wake_cancel
tools.description: Cancel one of your wake subscriptions.

tools.name: work_run
tools.description: Start long or detached work (a build, a test run, a job on another machine) so Backplane owns it: when it ends you are woken with its exit code and the end of its output; if a restart of Backplane cuts it off you are told it was lost and can start it again. Use this instead of `&`, nohup or disown, then end your turn; never poll or sleep-wait.

command.description: The shell command, run in this thread's folder.

lock.description: Optional named FIFO lock, held until work ends.

note.description: What it is, in a few words.

timeoutSec.description: Report a timeout after this many seconds; default 1200 (work.timeout.seconds setting), explicit 0 disables. Work keeps running; never killed.

tools.name: work_watch
tools.description: Have Backplane watch work that is already running and wake you when it ends: kind pid (a process) or file (a file that will contain the token this call returns). Then end your turn.

target.description: The pid, or the file's path.

timeoutSec.description: Report a timeout after this many seconds; default 1200 (work.timeout.seconds setting), explicit 0 disables. Never kills the watched work.

tools.name: lock_acquire
tools.description: Acquire a named FIFO lock without blocking; if queued, end your turn and wait for the grant message.

tools.name: lock_release
tools.description: Release your named lock, granting the next waiter.

tools.name: lock_cancel
tools.description: Leave a named lock queue.

tools.name: lock_list
tools.description: List named lock holders, timestamps, notes and FIFO waiters.

tools.name: work_list
tools.description: List the work Backplane watches for this thread (work_run and work_watch), with each one's state.

tools.name: work_cancel
tools.description: Stop work started with work_run (or a watched unit or pid). It shows as cancelling until its end is confirmed.

tools.name: work_unwatch
tools.description: Stop watching work without stopping it: it may still run, and you will not be told when it ends.

tools.name: review_comments
tools.description: The design review comments on this thread's design (a person's or an agent's, pinned to a place on a board layer or a schematic sheet): the open ones with their replies, and how many are resolved.

tools.name: review_comment
tools.description: Comment on the design, pinned to a place (op add: file, x, y in mm in the file's own coordinates, layer for a board, text), or answer (op add with parent), resolve, reopen, edit or drop a comment by its id. The person sees it pinned in the viewer.

op.description: add, resolve, reopen, edit or drop.

parent.description: The comment answered (an add that is a reply).

file.description: The board or schematic, from this thread's folder.

tools.name: preview_open
tools.description: Open the Backplane browser (the user sees it live in the app's Browser tab), optionally at a URL. Use it to check web UIs, datasheets, distributor pages and docs.

url.description: URL to load; a bare host gets https://, localhost gets http://.

tools.name: preview_navigate
tools.description: Go to a URL in the Backplane browser.

tools.name: preview_snapshot
tools.description: Read the page: URL, title, visible text, interactive elements and an outline whose [ref=eN] marks are targets for click and type. Snapshot before acting.

tools.name: preview_click
tools.description: Click an element (ref, locator or selector) or a point (x, y in viewport pixels).

ref.description: A ref from preview_snapshot's outline, e.g. e5 (preferred).

locator.description: A Playwright selector, role or text based, e.g. role=button[name='Send'] or text=Continue.

tools.name: preview_type
tools.description: Type text into an element (or the focused one).

ref.description: A ref from preview_snapshot's outline, e.g. e5 (preferred).

locator.description: A Playwright selector, role or text based, e.g. role=button[name='Send'] or text=Continue.

tools.name: preview_press
tools.description: Press a key (Enter, Escape, Tab, ArrowDown, Backspace, a...).

tools.name: preview_scroll
tools.description: Scroll the page (dx, dy in pixels; positive is right/down), or an element with a target.

ref.description: A ref from preview_snapshot's outline, e.g. e5 (preferred).

locator.description: A Playwright selector, role or text based, e.g. role=button[name='Send'] or text=Continue.

tools.name: preview_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the page and return its JSON value.

tools.name: preview_wait_for
tools.description: Wait until an element is visible, some text appears, or the URL contains a string.

ref.description: A ref from preview_snapshot's outline, e.g. e5 (preferred).

locator.description: A Playwright selector, role or text based, e.g. role=button[name='Send'] or text=Continue.

tools.name: preview_resize
tools.description: Resize the browser viewport.

tools.name: preview_status
tools.description: The browser's state: open, URL, title, viewport.

tools.name: kicad_ipc
tools.description: Send one command to the project's headless KiCad over its IPC API (Backplane starts one KiCad per project). path is the project's .kicad_pro, .kicad_pcb or .kicad_sch (absolute); type is the fully-qualified protobuf command, e.g. kiapi.board.commands.GetItems, kiapi.common.commands.BeginCommit, kiapi.backplane.SketchRoute; message is the command's fields as JSON. The answer is the response as JSON. Headless KiCad has no selection or view state: always pass explicit item IDs (the KIIDs GetItems returns), wrap edits in BeginCommit/EndCommit, then SaveDocument (the viewers follow the saved files). Unsaved work is undone with EndCommit CMA_DROP. Backplane KiCad bp.4 supports partial footprint updates and CreateItems from a symbol library id, with symbol libraries loaded on demand. On runtimes without footprint-partial-update or symbol-from-libid, the hub refuses unsafe requests and explains the workaround: send the full FootprintInstance from GetItems, or LoadAllLibraries, wait for GetLibraryStatuses, then PlaceSymbolFromLibrary. Selection, view and RunAction commands are refused at once. When IPC is unavailable the error says why and names the fallback (edit the file directly or use kicad-cli, then re-read the file).

path.description: Absolute path of the project's .kicad_pro, .kicad_pcb or .kicad_sch.

tools.name: kicad_ipc_status
tools.description: The project's headless KiCad: its server's state (starting, ready, failed or stopped), its version, its start command line (argv), and the capabilities and commands it has (kiapi.backplane.GetCapabilities). Starts the server if it is not running. Headless KiCad has no selection or view state: always pass explicit item IDs (KIIDs from GetItems) in kicad_ipc, wrap edits in BeginCommit/EndCommit, then SaveDocument.

path.description: Absolute path of the project's .kicad_pro, .kicad_pcb or .kicad_sch.

tools.name: permission_prompt
tools.description: Internal to Backplane: asks the user before a tool runs. Do not call it yourself.

tools.name: told_check
tools.description: Before telling the person something (a digest item, a reminder, news), check whether they were already told: by its topic key, or by text (matching words). Answers {told: bool, matches: [{key, text, channel, bot, at, ago}]}. Covers the last 7 days by default (up to 30) on this machine, including every alert already sent (asks, finished work, failures, merges, notify_person notes, which are recorded by themselves). Alerting is notify_person's policy (needs_you, done, or a routine's reminder or digest); this only tells you what was already said.

key.description: The topic key, e.g. lunch-dana-1028 (as given to told_mark).

text.description: The text you are about to say; matched by its words.

days.description: How many days back (default 7, at most 30).

tools.name: told_mark
tools.description: Record that you told the person something without an alert (in a digest, a room post, a chat answer, your Space, an email), so you and other bots skip it next time. Alerts, notify_person's included, are recorded by themselves. key: a short stable topic key (e.g. lunch-dana-1028); without one, it is made from the text. channel: digest, room, chat, email or other. Answers {key}.

key.description: A short stable topic key; made from the text when omitted.

text.description: What you told them, in a sentence.

channel.description: digest, room, chat, email or other (default chat).

tools.name: task_board_list
tools.description: List the shared task board: open items by default (all includes done and dropped). Answers {text, items}: text is one line per item, [status] title (id; @owner; %project; due D; group), and items has the full records.

status.description: todo, doing, blocked, done or dropped; several separated by commas.

owner.description: A bot's name or id, me for yourself, or person.

tools.name: task_board_add
tools.description: Add an item to the shared task board. Answers {id}.

title.description: What is to be done (at most 300 characters).

status.description: todo (default), doing, blocked, done or dropped.

owner.description: A bot's name or id, me for yourself, or person (default).

links.description: URLs, thread ids or paths: a JSON array, or a string split on spaces and commas (at most 20).

tools.name: task_board_update
tools.description: Change an item on the task board: only the fields you give change. Answers {id}.

status.description: todo, doing, blocked, done or dropped.

owner.description: A bot's name or id, me for yourself, or person.

links.description: Replaces the links: a JSON array, or a string split on spaces and commas.

notes_append.description: A line added to the notes.

tools.name: task_board_remove
tools.description: Delete an item from the task board for good. Prefer task_board_update with status dropped, which keeps a record.

tools.name: task_board_import
tools.description: Import a markdown todo list (checkbox items `- [ ]`, `- [x]`, `- [~]`; headings become groups). Lines without a checkbox are not imported and are returned as `skipped`. Importing the same list again adds nothing. Answers {added, duplicates, skipped}.

project.description: Put every item in this project (a name or id).

owner.description: A bot's name or id, me for yourself, or person (default).

tools.name: order_review
tools.description: The project's manufacturing review. gate (a buy thread, before exporting): Backplane checks the review and, unless it is current and passed, shows the person why and asks them; answers what it did. check: whether the design (its boards, schematics, models and fab files) was reviewed since it last changed; answers state (none, stale or current), verdict, summary and issues. record: after a manufacturing review, keep its verdict (ok or issues), a one-line summary and the issues, one short line each, with the design as it is now.

issues.description: record: what must change, one short line each ("Shade: walls 0.6 mm, need 0.8"), at most 8; none when ok.
